# Spoken 0.2.0 — Test Build 14
A refined workbench, reliable document splitting, and a compact menu bar. This is an Apple Silicon test pre-release. The app reports version **0.2.0 (14)**.
## What's new
- Drag Summary, Action Items, transcripts and other document tabs into either half of a view to arrange them side by side. Moving tabs preserves document sessions and unsaved edits. The whole tab is clickable and draggable. - Consistent toolbar hover and pressed feedback for Info, Share, document actions, split controls and tab close buttons. Sharing continues to use the native macOS share picker and includes the visible draft. - A simpler meeting start screen with recording and audio import actions. Recording controls in the main window include pause, resume and stop. - A compact menu bar with recording, Copy Last Dictation, and one Dictation Options submenu. Active processing and provider warnings stay accessible. - Dictation and meeting transcription use built-in FluidAudio speech models; legacy oMLX audio selections fall back to the built-in provider. Configured text and vision providers remain available for cleanup and workflows. - Refined native Icon Composer artwork and a more compact dictation overlay. On macOS 26, icon appearance follows the system's icon appearance setting.
## Update an existing installation
**Builds 9 and newer:** open Spoken and choose **Check for Updates…** from the Spoken menu, or use the update action when it appears in the sidebar. Download and install the update, then let Spoken restart. Finish any active recording or dictation before restarting. Existing library content is preserved.
Older builds may use the standard Sparkle update window for this upgrade. Builds 8 and older use an unsupported pre-library storage format and are excluded from this update. Keep those installations and their data intact.
## Fresh installation
Download the DMG, drag **Spoken** to **Applications**, eject the DMG, then open Spoken from Applications. The download contains the release app, not Spoken Dev. Requires an Apple Silicon Mac; macOS 15 or newer is the supported test target.
This test build is **ad-hoc signed, not Developer ID signed or notarized**. macOS may require **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway** on first launch. Microphone, accessibility or screen-recording permissions may need to be granted again. The in-app update archive is authenticated with Sparkle's EdDSA signature.
## Known limitations
- Cross-device installation and update acceptance still require tester feedback. - The menu-bar download badge, expanded speech-model catalog, and UI localization are not included in this build. - The Spoken Library is local but not encrypted. Project Privacy restricts agent access; it does not encrypt files or protect exported copies.

# Spoken 0.1.0 Alpha 1 — Test Build 13
This invited alpha test build brings the redesigned transcript workbench and protects edits across closing and restarting the app.
## What's new
- New adaptive black-and-white app icon and matching menu-bar symbols for ready, recording, paused, and processing states. The running app and About panel follow the system light/dark appearance automatically.
- Open documents in tabs and arrange them in two resizable views. Transcript playback and speaker controls use a more compact toolbar; meetings show transcripts, output documents, and images in the sidebar. - Share documents through the native macOS Share menu. Markdown and meeting exports remain available in document actions. Copy, Share, and Markdown export use the visible draft while editing. - A blue tab dot marks unsaved edits. Command-S saves; closing a dirty tab, window, or the app offers Save, Discard Changes, and Cancel. Failed saves keep your draft open, and regeneration cannot overwrite newer saved work. - Tabs and split layouts reopen after restart. Unsaved document and transcript drafts have private local recovery copies, separate from saved revisions. - Project Privacy is available in each project's actions menu. Protected folders carry a lock badge and explain which agent profiles may read them. This controls MCP access, not library encryption or copies you share/export. - The sidebar Update action can accept an already discovered update directly. The app also refuses to quit for an update while recording or finalizing dictation; finish the capture and then retry the restart.
## Installation and compatibility
Builds 9 and newer may update through **Spoken → Check for Updates…**. Build 12's scheduled-update sidebar may still open the standard Sparkle window for this upgrade; proceed there. The corrected sidebar flow is included in Build 13 for future upgrades.
For a fresh installation, open the DMG, drag **Spoken** to **Applications**, eject the DMG, and open the installed app. This Apple Silicon test build is ad-hoc signed and **not notarized**. macOS may require **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**, and permissions may need to be granted again.
Builds 8 and older use a pre-library format that this version does not import. They are excluded from the update feed. Keep that installation and its data.
## Remaining alpha limitations
- Draft recovery follows a short 600 ms debounce; abrupt termination can lose the latest edits within that interval. Playback and reading positions are not restored. - A recovered draft in another project may need to be opened and reviewed before Save All can finish. Conflicts keep the draft rather than overwriting. - Cross-device update/install acceptance and native tab dragging still need additional testing. The menu-bar download badge is not part of this build.
This is an invited test pre-release, not the supported notarized alpha release.

# Spoken 0.1.0 Alpha 1 — Test Build 12
Test Build 12 includes the installer, setup, speech-model progress, and Notch legibility fixes from Build 11. It adds a quieter in-app update flow for future test builds.
## What changed
- When a later update is available, a blue download icon appears next to Settings in the sidebar. Click it to reveal **Update**, then click **Update** to start the download. - The sidebar shows download percentage from Sparkle's received bytes, then **Installing**. Sparkle verifies the archive, installs it, and relaunches Spoken. Errors and permission prompts continue to use Sparkle's standard dialogs. - Scheduled update checks no longer interrupt work with a modal alert. The menu command **Spoken → Check for Updates…** remains available.
## Installation and current update
Existing installs on Test Build 9 or newer can update directly to Build 12 through **Spoken → Check for Updates…**. The first update uses the standard Sparkle window because the older installed app does not yet contain the new sidebar control. The sidebar control becomes available for subsequent updates.
For a new installation, open the DMG, drag **Spoken** to **Applications**, eject the DMG, then open Spoken from **Applications**. Keep only that installed copy running. This invited test build is ad-hoc signed and not notarized; macOS may require **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway** on first launch and may ask for permissions again when replacing an older ad-hoc signed build.
Builds 8 and older use a pre-library data format this build does not import. They are excluded from this in-app update and should keep their data and older installation until a migration is available. This is still an unsigned alpha test build for Apple Silicon Macs, not the supported notarized release.

# Spoken 0.1.0 Alpha 1 — Test Build 11
Test Build 11 replaces Test Build 10 for new testers. It contains the first-run, model setup, and Notch contrast fixes from Build 10, plus a clearer installer.
## What changed
- The DMG opens as a familiar drag-to-Applications Finder window: large Spoken and Applications icons, an arrow, and English instructions. License and release documents remain inside the disk image but do not crowd the window. - The Notch recording panel keeps its labels and controls legible in Light appearance. - The screen-recording permission step closes the current Spoken process and asks you to reopen the installed app. It no longer creates a second process. Only the app needs to restart, not the Mac. - The built-in speech model starts downloading after permission setup, so the app restart cannot interrupt it. Setup displays download or preparation progress and no longer loads the model into memory just to complete setup.
## Installation
1. Quit every running Spoken copy. Open the DMG, drag **Spoken** to **Applications**, and replace an older test build if macOS asks. Your existing Spoken Library remains in place. 2. Eject the DMG. Open Spoken from **Applications**, not from the mounted disk image. Keep only this installed copy running. 3. This invited test build is ad-hoc signed and not notarized. After the first launch attempt, macOS may require **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**. It may ask for permissions again when replacing an older ad-hoc signed build. 4. Follow setup. The built-in speech model downloads on first installation; time depends on the network and Mac. Dictation and meeting transcription then run locally.
This build is for Apple Silicon Macs. Installs on Test Build 9 or newer can receive it through Spoken's in-app updater; open **Spoken → Check for Updates…** to check immediately. The standard Sparkle update window offers the download and restart. A manual DMG download remains available.
Builds 8 and older used the pre-library data format, which this build does not import. They are excluded from this in-app update and should keep their data and older installation until an explicit migration is available. The supported alpha still requires Developer ID signing, notarization, and second-device validation.
## Verification
The Swift suite passed 415 tests with two skipped and no failures for the Build 10 app fixes. The Build 11 archive passed the release binary check, strict code-signature verification, checksum validation, and Finder inspection of the compressed DMG.

# Spoken 0.1.0 Alpha 1 — Test Build 5
Test Build 5 replaces Test Build 4, which passed static signature validation but could not launch after installation because its ad-hoc app signature enabled Hardened Runtime library validation for the bundled Sparkle framework.
## What is new
- Meeting capture returns to idle as soon as the authoritative Mic/System audio and timeline are safely stored. Transcription, review, flows, and the derived playback mix continue independently. - The Notch guides a compact speaker review with stable audio samples, naming, previous/next navigation, source-specific speaker counts, and optional proposal-based re-diarization. - Project flows are shown and approved per meeting before they run. Failed flows can be retried individually, and provider/model routing errors are now actionable. - Audio can be dropped directly onto a project or imported from its project action without first creating an empty meeting. - “Open in Hub” restores the Spoken window and opens the exact meeting transcript or outstanding review. - Hidden meeting recordings briefly reveal their Mic/System activity every five minutes as a quiet reminder that capture is still running. - Screenshot notes remain open until they are attached, skipped, or dismissed. - The read-only Spoken MCP helper and existing local project access controls remain included.
## Fixed since Test Build 4
- The unsigned invited-tester package now launches correctly from Applications. Its app, bundled MCP helper, and Sparkle components use a consistent ad-hoc signing mode without Developer ID-only library validation.
## Installation
1. Download the DMG. 2. Drag Spoken into Applications. 3. Because this test build is not notarized, Control-click Spoken and choose Open. If macOS still blocks it, use System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway.
## Important
This build uses an ad-hoc code signature and is not notarized. It is intended only for invited alpha testing on Apple Silicon Macs. Local oMLX or Ollama routes must be running when selected; enterprise or cloud-compatible routes must be configured explicitly. The supported alpha release will use Developer ID signing and Apple notarization.

# Spoken 0.1.0 Alpha 1 — Test Build 3
This is the first complete Spoken build with in-app updates.
## What is included
- `Check for Updates…` in the Spoken app menu. - Software Update controls in General Settings. - EdDSA-authenticated Sparkle updates on the alpha channel. - The read-only Spoken MCP helper and the current alpha workbench.
## Installation
1. Download the DMG. 2. Drag Spoken into Applications. 3. Because this test build is not notarized, Control-click Spoken and choose Open. If macOS still blocks it, use System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway.
After this one-time installation, future alpha test builds can be installed from Spoken → Check for Updates….
## Important
This build uses an ad-hoc code signature and is not notarized. It is intended only for invited alpha testing on Apple Silicon Macs. The final alpha release will use Developer ID signing and Apple notarization.
